items.headline: Can you park on a Burlington street overnight?
items.deck: Usually no. Most streets have a 1 to 6 a.m. parking ban, but exemptions and a paid citywide permit can make overnight parking legal.
items.label: Parking
items.alt: Illustration of a car parked on a Burlington residential street at night beside a clock.
items.storyGoal: Give Burlington drivers the exact overnight parking rule and clearly separate occasional exemptions from the recurring residential permit.

items.deck: There are five. Three are on Guelph Line, and running one of them can cost $325.
items.label: Road safety
items.alt: Illustration of a red traffic light and roadside camera at a Burlington intersection.
items.storyGoal: Create a definitive Burlington search page listing every current red-light camera, the penalty and how the cameras trigger.

items.headline: Do you need a permit for a shed in Burlington?
items.deck: Not always. The building-permit threshold is 15 square metres, but a small shed still has to follow zoning rules.
items.label: Home rules
items.alt: Illustration of a backyard shed with measurement lines and a 15-square-metre permit threshold.
items.storyGoal: Answer the Burlington shed-permit question directly, then separate the 15-square-metre building-permit exemption from zoning and property-specific approvals.
items.verificationTier: Primary City of Burlington building and zoning sources

items.storyGoal: Explain what Burlington's more than $90 million in stormwater investment has physically changed, using Tuck Creek as a concrete example while being explicit about unfinished and paused work.
